task: Read-only review of rotation normalization, exact cardinal transforms, room contact and operation boundaries

findings.title: Intermediate displacement rounding can erase a sub-ULP room overhang
findings.description: With subject.x=2e-16, camera.x=-3, room.subjectX=3 and yaw=0, the exact final camera coordinate is -2e-16 m. The intermediate subtraction rounds to -3, giving displayed/model xFromLeft=0, insideRoom=true, outsideCount=0. The exact final coordinate is representable, but the intermediate displacement is not.
findings.acceptanceAssessment: Observed numerical limitation only; no material workflow failure established. The displacement is 5,000,000 times smaller than the contract 1e-9 numeric-readout round-trip tolerance and 5,000,000,000 times smaller than the 1e-6 m bounded display threshold. Those are readout constraints, not permission to relax containment; no separate general room-coordinate error budget was found in the scoped contract. Existing one-ULP cardinal-roll fixture uses a different geometry and was inspected, not executed. Preserve this evidence; do not change geometry or tolerances for this batch.

tests.result: NaN/+infinity/-infinity room rotations returned false without mutation; SceneTransform rotations rejected each with invalidTransform. Room deltas greatestFiniteMagnitude, negative greatestFiniteMagnitude, 180 and 720 normalized from yaw 45 to valid 173, -83, -135 and 45 degrees. Scene boundary light (100,2,-100) rotated successfully at 90,-90,180,-180,360,450,-450 degrees with exact signed boundary coordinates. Room sub-ULP case reproduced x=0/inside rather than exact -2e-16.

Standalone and arranged scene rotations check nonfinite inputs before copying/transforming, reduce finite angles modulo 360, use exact cardinal coefficients, retain original coordinate terms and validate completed scenes. Room rotation checks complete validity before mutation; cardinal room-yaw coefficients are exact. Existing RoomRotationTests covers invalid/huge deltas and two-half-turn geometry; RoomCardinalRollContactTests covers wall/floor/ceiling contact, a one-representable-step wall overhang, and adjacent noncardinal components. No test suite, native runtime or physical placement execution performed.

outcome: No confirmed material rotation or room-contact workflow defect in this narrow review. One reproducible informational IEEE rounding limitation retained. No repository edits, commits, documentation/state updates or full-suite run; generic mirror issue excluded as requested.
